species.look_here_first: Start with the comb-like branches and the hairy leaf bases. Hairy grama is a tufted perennial with narrow leaves bearing conspicuous papillose-based hairs, usually 1–4 one-sided pectinate branches, and a naked branch tip extending beyond the terminal spikelets.

species.look_here_first: For CANADA goldenrod, compare the mid-stem leaf TOOTH pattern and the lower/upper stem hairs with S. altissima; Canada commonly has finer, often more regularly toothed thinner 3-nerved leaves and sparser/longer stem hair than tall goldenrod. However overlap is extreme and some variants of both break these patterns. S. gigantea is the smoother/waxy lower stem one. Photograph lower stem, an entire leaf face/underside and flowering branches on SAME plant.

species.look_here_first: FIRST photograph the entire mature flowering array (when not recently mowed): this inland Texas annual/short-lived saltmarsh aster has VERY OPEN, diffuse, wiry branching with wide negative space between many small heads. Check mostly sessile narrow linear leaves, near-hairless stems and taprooted base. TRUE eastern S. subulatum usually has denser, more upper-pyramidal heads in coastal/saline SE Texas. Mowing and damaged plants can distort architecture; don't use flower color or one head alone. This species is NOT Eurybia divaricata (white wood aster).
